body: Off-by-one: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` overcounts whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 shows "1/2"). Then `showingLast` is false on the real last page, and clicking Next sets offset = user_count, which loads an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

`group.users.delete(user_id)` skips the existing `Group#remove`/`destroy_deletions` logic. On a has_many :through it delete_all's the GroupUser rows without callbacks, so the user's `primary_group_id` is never cleared (they keep the group flair/title after removal), and the `user_count` counter_cache may not be decremented. Load the user and call `group.remove(user)` (plus the primary_group_id reset) instead. Also, `group.save` afterwards does nothing useful here.

`group.add(user)` does `users.push(user)` with no membership check. Adding a username that is already in the group violates the unique index on group_users(group_id, user_id) and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is a 500. In the new UI this is easy to hit, since the admin just types usernames and presses Add. Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`, or check for an existing GroupUser.

This is a public (non-admin) endpoint, and `limit` comes straight from the client with no upper bound. `?limit=1000000` on a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0) serializes every user in one request. Negative `limit`/`offset` values also reach Postgres (`OFFSET must not be negative`), which is a 500. Clamp both, e.g. `limit = [[limit, 1].max, 200].min` and `offset = [offset, 0].max`.

The offset is clamped against the client's cached `user_count`. After removing the only member on the last page, the reload asks for offset == old total and gets an empty page: offset isn't moved back, and the pager shows e.g. "3/2". Recompute or clamp the offset against the new total after a removal.

`findMembers()` is now fired from setupController without being returned or awaited, and the `offset` stored on the model is never reset. Navigating away and back to a group keeps the old page offset, and the old member list stays on screen until the request finishes. Consider resetting `offset` to 0 and returning the promise from afterModel/model.

After a successful add, `usernames` is never cleared (the TODO acknowledges this), so clicking Add again re-submits the same users. Combined with the server-side duplicate-insert issue in add_members, that second click produces a 500. Clear `usernames` in the promise's then().

This spec calls `remove_member` with `:put`, but the route is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`, so it doesn't exercise the real verb. Use `xhr :delete`. Also, the automatic-group specs depend on a group with id 1 existing (a seeded automatic group). Create one explicitly with `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` so the test doesn't rely on seed data.
